doc.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022

title: Memorable gigs: Red Rocks, Carnegie Hall, orchestras and chills
summary: Best gigs were with Mangione, plus Eastman lab band and Michigan State marching band moments, and Bartok's Miraculous Mandarin.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: How about a gig that you played that either you recall as being the absolute Mount Everest of gigs, or the exact opposite. like this is such a train wreck?

Oh I don’t know. Let’s see. I think some of things I did with Chuck were really good because there were so many people there. Like the Red Rocks concert was really good. Red Rocks in Colorado. And you know I made a special trip to be there to play that, or he had me come you know. And so that was really good just because of the electricity that was going on. And actually the other ones we did in various places with Chuck, we did them in big halls in Boston and New York, Carnegie Hall in New York, and D.C. So those things were very, very big. But I tell you, you know when things are really going I get the chills. I can feel it. And I’ve had it happen, you know, when I was directing the lab band at Eastman, the third band. You know? And when they were playing Jeez, I mean one concert I just wow, just got knocked out. When I was at Michigan State I had to have a scholarship in the fall, I had to play in the marching band. I remember one time in that stupid marching band, you know, just getting the chills, playing the stuff that we were playing for, you know, 80,000 people. So it happens, you know, like it happens when you play in a new orchestra you know just like playing “Miraculous Mandarin” by Bartok. I really get, mmm, this is great.
